title: Sins of Omission
definition: The doctrine of Sins of Omission teaches that sin includes not only doing what God forbids, but failing to do the good He commands.
summary: Sins of Omission names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. sin includes not only doing what God forbids, but failing to do the good He commands. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Sins of Omission because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: sin includes not only doing what God forbids, but failing to do the good He commands. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people can feel righteous because they avoided scandal while neglecting mercy, obedience, witness, or love. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask where obedience has been delayed or ignored. Follow Christ in active faith, not merely in avoiding obvious wrong. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
